reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The request counts "attempts that do not land" and lists "collision with another landing" as a failure category. The reading narrowed "did not land" to records that are Rejected or Failed. An attempt that passed verification but failed to land (the drain's LandStep::NotLanded) counts only if its job closed with a non-landed outcome; if it is still blocked or open, it does not count. So a line can have two collision attempts and never be diagnosed. (round 1 of 5). The plan reuses group_lines and line_attempts properly. It keeps prompt budgets unchanged by checking the new frame against the verifier budget set, as the critic's frame is, and it bounds diagnosis spend with a create_new claim. Four design problems need fixing before code is written. (1) Filing the diagnosis invocation under the line's last job, which is already closed, breaks the landing gate's check that a closed job's totals match its invocation records (athena-gate reconcile.rs:105-131). It also adds the diagnosis cost to that job's spend and score. The steward's pattern (a fresh run id routed in store.rs) should be the design, not a fallback. (2) The retry follow-up joins the original line. When the scope guard has paused that line, which the plan's risks say is the usual case at two failures, the core refuses both the reading (reading.rs:1112) and the dispatch (run/mod.rs:1012). The drain's own-follow-up exception does not get past this, and the fake cannot show it. (3) Counting only Rejected or Failed records leaves out verified-but-not-landed attempts (collision), which the request names as a category, whenever their job is still blocked or open. (4) Every drain demonstration uses a fake whose line standing it computes itself. No test checks the real drain step reading real records, and the drain part of criterion 9 cannot fail. Athena's findings about files outside the deliverables are mostly files the change must touch to compile; I weighed them as minor.
